title: Global EV Market Monitor: Trucks and Buses (Q1 2026) - International Council on Clean Transportation
source_name: 国际清洁交通委员会 ICCT
content: An overview of the global zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicle market Market Spotlight Global EV Market Monitor: Trucks and Buses (Q1 2026) China still leading in sales by a large margin Zero-emission truck and bus sales grew from 75,834 units in 2020 to 525,486 in 2025; sales reached 101,418 in Q1 2026 alone. China supplied 85% of the Q1 2026 total. Europe and India climb into second and third place China remained the leading market for zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicle sales, with 86,129 units sold, up 34% from Q1 2025. The European Union ranked second with 6,387 units, a year-on-year increase of 42%, followed by India with 2,892, an increase of 85%. The United States recorded a 57% decline in sales, to 2,483, and ranked fourth. Japan moved ahead of the United Kingdom into fifth place, with sales rising 23% to 880 units, while sales in the United Kingdom fell by 25% to 732. Norway and Switzerland both recorded 358 units, representing a year-on-year increase of 25% for Norway and 77% for Switzerland (the strongest growth in the group after India). Buses are electrifying faster than trucks in most markets In 35 of the 43 markets covered, the zero-emission share of buses was higher than that of trucks. In some cases, the gap was significant: Chile reached a 68.5% zero-emission share for buses against a 0.4% share for trucks, while the United Kingdom recorded a 54.2% share for buses against 0.9% for trucks; similar patterns were recorded in Sweden and Portugal. China departed from this trend, recording a 24.2% share for trucks against a 14.3% share for buses, reflecting lower penetration of electric coaches while city buses are almost fully electrified. Globally, the two segments had similar zero-emission shares as of Q1 2026, of 12.4% for buses and 10.4% for trucks, but trucks accounted for 88,579 of the 101,418 zero-emission vehicles sold in Q1 2026. Chinese automakers swept the top truck manufacturers; the bus market is mixed All ten of the largest zero-emission truck manufacturers in Q1 2026 were Chinese, led by Sinotruk (9,033 units), XCMG (8,049), and Foton (6,946). Together, the top 10 automakers accounted for 56,856 units, or 75% of the truck volume attributable to a named manufacturer. The list of top bus manufacturers was more mixed: Yutong led with 1,798 units, followed by King Long (1,513) and CRRC (1,498), but five of the top 10 were non-Chinese, including PMI (642), Ashok Leyland (587), and Volkswagen Group (543). The leading truck maker sold 5 times as many units as the leading bus maker in Q1 2026.
